title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day From Earth After Nearly 50 Years
title_zh: 飞行近五十年，旅行者1号抵达距地球“一光日”里程碑
source_name: NASA — “NASA’s Voyager 1 Makes History, Reaching One Light-Day From Earth”
summary_zh: 2026年11月18日，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）的“旅行者1号”探测器创造了历史，成为首个距离地球达到“一光日”的人造物体。发射升空49年多后，它如今距地球约259亿公里（约161亿英里），无线电信号单程传输就需要整整24小时，一次一来一回的通信延迟高达48小时。文章介绍了旅行者1号从探测木星和土星、于2012年进入星际空间至今的漫长旅程，并说明工程师如何应对核动力逐年衰减的挑战，通过逐步关闭部分仪器和借助深空网络70米巨型天线，让这艘高龄探测器继续传回宝贵数据。
paragraphs: On 18 November 2026, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a historic milestone by becoming the first human-made object to travel one light-day away from Earth. More than 49 years after its launch in September 1977, the probe is now about 25.9 billion kilometres, or 16.1 billion miles, from our planet. That distance is roughly 173 times the average distance between Earth and the Sun.

A light-day is the distance that light travels in 24 hours, moving at nearly 300,000 kilometres per second. Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, this milestone has a very practical effect on mission control. Any command sent by engineers on Earth now takes a full 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. Waiting for Voyager 1's reply takes another 24 hours, creating a 48-hour delay for a single round-trip conversation.

Voyager 1 was originally designed to explore the outer planets, sending back detailed images and data from Jupiter and Saturn. Instead of stopping there, the spacecraft kept flying outward toward the edge of the solar system. In 2012, it crossed into interstellar space, the vast region between the stars. Today, it continues to send valuable measurements from an environment that no other spacecraft has explored for so long.

Keeping such an old machine working at this extreme distance is a constant engineering challenge. Managed by NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the probe relies on plutonium power generators that lose around four watts of electrical power each year. To protect its tight energy budget, engineers have gradually turned off several instruments over the years so that essential systems can stay active. Back on Earth, NASA's Deep Space Network uses giant 70-metre antennas in California, Spain and Australia to catch the spacecraft's faint radio signal.

Although Voyager 1's power supply will eventually run too low to keep its transmitters working, the spacecraft will continue drifting through space for millions of years. Even as communication slows down to a two-day wait, every tiny signal helps scientists understand the space beyond our solar system. Reaching one light-day is not only a record for distance, but also a reminder of how far careful engineering and long-term scientific curiosity can reach.
paragraphs_zh: 2026年11月18日，美国国家航空航天局（NASA）的“旅行者1号”探测器迎来了一座历史性里程碑，成为首个飞抵距离地球“一光日”位置的人造物体。自1977年9月发射升空已过去49年多，这艘探测器如今距离我们的星球约259亿公里（约161亿英里），这一距离大约是地球与太阳之间平均距离的173倍。
“一光日”是指光以每秒近30万公里的速度在24小时内行进的距离。由于无线电信号以光速传播，这一里程碑对任务控制中心产生了非常实际的影响。如今，地球上的工程师发出的任何指令都需要整整24小时才能抵达探测器，而等待“旅行者1号”传回回应还需要另外24小时，从而使一次往返通信出现长达48小时的延迟。
“旅行者1号”最初的设计目标是探索太阳系外围行星，曾传回来自木星和土星的精细图像与数据。但它并未止步于此，而是继续向外飞行，奔向太阳系的边缘。2012年，它跨入了恒星之间广阔的星际空间。如今，它仍在从这个从未有其他航天器探索过如此之久的环境中，持续发回宝贵的测量数据。
在如此遥远的极端距离下，让一台如此高龄的机器保持运转是一项持续不断的工程挑战。这艘由NASA喷气推进实验室管理的探测器依赖钚燃料发电机供电，但电源每年都会损失约4瓦电力。为了守住紧张的能源预算，工程师们多年来逐步关闭了多台仪器，好让核心系统继续工作。而在地球上，NASA的深空网络动用位于美国加利福尼亚州、西班牙和澳大利亚的70米巨型天线，来捕捉这艘探测器传来的微弱无线电信号。
尽管“旅行者1号”的电力供应最终会耗得太低，无法再维持发射机运转，但这艘探测器仍将在太空中继续漂流数百万年。即便如今通信已经慢到需要等待两天，每一个微小的信号依然在帮助科学家认识太阳系之外的宇宙空间。抵达“一光日”不仅刷新了距离纪录，也提醒着我们：严谨的工程技术与长久的科学探索精神能够走多远。

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
options: NASA's plan to launch a faster replacement for Voyager 1 within the next five years.
Voyager 1 reaching one light-day from Earth, how that distance affects communication, and how NASA keeps the probe operating.
Why Voyager 1 failed to send back clear images during its early visits to Jupiter and Saturn.
How NASA's Deep Space Network built new 70-metre antennas in 2026 to repair Voyager 1.
questions.explanation: 全文围绕“旅行者1号”抵达距地球一光日的历史性里程碑展开，介绍了这一距离如何带来48小时的通信延迟、它进入星际空间的历程，以及NASA如何依靠节省能源和深空网络维持其运行。其他选项在原文中均未提及或与原文不符。

evidence.quote: On 18 November 2026, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a historic milestone by becoming the first human-made object to travel one light-day away from Earth.

questions.prompt: According to the second paragraph, why does a round-trip communication with Voyager 1 take 48 hours?
options: Because engineers only check signals from the spacecraft once every two days.
Because the spacecraft stops its transmitters for 24 hours between each message to save energy.
Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, taking 24 hours each way.
Because signals must pass through Jupiter and Saturn before reaching Earth.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred from the fourth paragraph about how NASA manages Voyager 1's declining power?
options: Engineers have prioritized essential systems by shutting down some instruments as power drops.
NASA has found a way to recharge the probe's plutonium generators using radio antennas.
All of Voyager 1's original instruments are still operating at full electrical power.
The Deep Space Network can only receive signals from Voyager 1 when it passes near Australia.
